intro: In the last lesson you took part in discussions and took turns. Meetings at work need a few more tools: how to **interrupt politely** (and stop others interrupting you), how to **clarify and summarise**, and how to give a **clear progress update** on your project. Warm-up: in your last meeting, did you want to say something but didn't?
teachingNotes: This functional lesson builds on b2-discussion (turn-taking, inviting others: What do you think, Sari?; pros and cons; speculating), b1-giving-opinions (I see what you mean, but …; 'I agree', never 'I am agree'), b2-vocab-work-business (agenda, the minutes, action points, follow up, on track / behind schedule / ahead of schedule, discuss with no 'about') and b1-problems-calls (Can you hear me?, You're on mute, you're breaking up, Could you say that again?). Recap those in a line; don't re-teach them. New here: interrupting and holding the floor, clarifying, checking understanding and summarising, and a structured progress update. Contexts: a startup in Jakarta, a bank in Surabaya, Zoom / Google Meet stand-ups, Pak Hasan and Bu Ani as managers.

Interrupting: a soft start + a small request + your point, quickly: Sorry to interrupt, but … / Could I just add something? / If I could just come in here, … (a phrase to remember: don't analyse could + if) / Sorry to jump in, but … (a bit informal). 'just' makes the request sound small. The node's common error is 'Sorry, I want to cut.' (from 'Maaf, saya potong') → 'Sorry to interrupt, but could I just add something?'. Why: 'cut' alone means memotong (paper, costs); the phrasal verb 'cut in' does exist (Sorry to cut in), so never mark 'cut in' wrong; and 'I want to …' sounds like a demand. Also 'Sorry before' (maaf sebelumnya) isn't English. 'Excuse me, can I say something?' is understandable but less smooth: don't mark it wrong. Culture: many Indonesians wait until the boss or an older colleague finishes (sungkan); in English meetings a short, polite interruption with a good reason is normal, and saying nothing is often taken as agreement. Too direct: Wait! / Stop! / Don't cut me.

Holding the floor (mempertahankan giliran bicara): Just let me finish this point. / Bear with me for a second. (= please wait patiently; spelled bear, not bare; nothing to do with the animal) / I'll come to that in a minute. Giving the turn back: Sorry, go ahead. Online: when two people start at once, Sorry, go ahead / No, you go first. Recap from b1-problems-calls only: You're on mute, Can everyone see my screen? (new but simple).

Clarifying and summarising: Sorry, could you clarify what you mean by …? / What exactly do you mean by …? / Sorry, I'm not sure I follow. Checking understanding (say it back in your own words): So what you're saying is …? / Just to be clear, …? ('Just to be sure' is also fine). Summarising: So, to sum up, … / Let me recap the action points (Indonesian 'rekap' helps) / Let's go over the action points. summarise (British) / summarize (American). Traps: 'Meaning?' (from 'Maksudnya?') is too blunt; 'What do you mean?' alone, with a flat tone, can sound like a challenge, so add Sorry + by + the word; 'Can you repeat again?' says 'again' twice → Could you say that again? / Could you repeat that?. 'In conclusion' belongs to essays and formal talks: in a meeting 'So, to sum up' sounds more natural. That's a tendency: don't mark 'In conclusion' wrong in speech.

Progress updates: status + done + now + next + risk. Status: We're on track / ahead of schedule / slightly behind schedule / a week behind schedule. Done: present perfect with no finished time (We've completed the design. We've already tested it on Android.), but past simple with a finished time (We finished the design last week; not *We've finished it last week). Now: present continuous (We're currently working on the payment page. We're waiting for the client's feedback.). Next: The next step is to … / Next week we're going to …. Risk: The main risk is that the supplier might be late. Traps: no tense marking ('sudah selesai' → *We already finish → We've already finished); 'sedang' → be + -ing (*We working on); Indonesian office English 'masih on progress' → It's still in progress / We're still working on it; progress is uncountable (We've made good progress, not *a good progress / *progresses); 'actually' = sebenarnya, not 'saat ini' (Indonesian aktual) → currently. American speakers often say 'We already finished it': accept it in free speech, but teach the present perfect.

Limits: A0–B1 grammar plus the chain (no third conditional, wish, past modals like must have, participle clauses, non-defining relative clauses, causative, future perfect or advanced passive). Don't teach chairing a meeting (opening, managing the agenda, closing), writing formal minutes, negotiating or presentation language. Listening items use one voice and no speaker labels. Correct one thing at a time, usually 'I want to cut', 'on progress', 'Can you repeat again?' or 'We've finished it last week'.

keyPoints.title: Interrupt politely and hold the floor
keyPoints.explanation: To interrupt, use a soft start, a small request and then make your point quickly: Sorry to interrupt, but … / Could I just add something? / If I could just come in here, …. Not 'Sorry, I want to cut': cut alone means memotong (you can say Sorry to cut in). When someone interrupts you and you want to finish, hold the floor: Just let me finish this point. / Bear with me for a second. / I'll come to that in a minute. Then give the turn back: Sorry, go ahead.

examples.en: Sorry to interrupt, but could I just add something about the price?
examples.id: Maaf menyela, tapi boleh saya menambahkan sesuatu soal harganya?

examples.en: Just let me finish this point, and then you can ask questions.
examples.id: Biarkan saya menyelesaikan poin ini dulu, lalu kalian boleh bertanya.

examples.en: Bear with me for a second. The file is still opening.
examples.id: Mohon sabar sebentar. Filenya masih terbuka.

id.title: Menyela dengan sopan dan mempertahankan giliran bicara
id.explanation: Untuk menyela, pakai pembuka yang halus, permintaan kecil, lalu sampaikan poinmu dengan cepat: Sorry to interrupt, but … / Could I just add something? / If I could just come in here, …. Bukan 'Sorry, I want to cut': cut saja artinya memotong (kalau mau, bilang Sorry to cut in). Kalau orang lain menyela dan kamu ingin selesai dulu, pertahankan giliranmu: Just let me finish this point. / Bear with me for a second. / I'll come to that in a minute. Lalu kembalikan gilirannya: Sorry, go ahead.

keyPoints.title: Clarify, check and summarise
keyPoints.explanation: When something isn't clear, ask about the exact word: Sorry, could you clarify what you mean by …? / What exactly do you mean by …?. To check you've understood, say it back in your own words: So what you're saying is …? / Just to be clear, …?. At the end, summarise: So, to sum up, … / Let me recap the action points. Avoid 'Meaning?' (too blunt) and 'Can you repeat again?' (repeat already means again).

examples.en: Sorry, could you clarify what you mean by 'phase two'?
examples.id: Maaf, bisa diperjelas apa maksud Anda dengan 'tahap dua'?

examples.en: So what you're saying is that the client wants a cheaper version?
examples.id: Jadi maksud Anda, kliennya ingin versi yang lebih murah?

examples.en: Let me recap the action points before we finish.
examples.id: Saya rekap poin tindak lanjutnya sebelum kita selesai.

id.title: Mengklarifikasi, mengecek dan merangkum
id.explanation: Kalau ada yang tidak jelas, tanyakan kata yang persis: Sorry, could you clarify what you mean by …? / What exactly do you mean by …?. Untuk mengecek bahwa kamu sudah paham, ulangi dengan kata-katamu sendiri: So what you're saying is …? / Just to be clear, …?. Di akhir, rangkum: So, to sum up, … / Let me recap the action points. Hindari 'Meaning?' (terlalu ketus) dan 'Can you repeat again?' (repeat sudah berarti mengulang lagi).

keyPoints.title: Give a clear progress update
keyPoints.explanation: A clear update has up to five parts: the status (We're on track / slightly behind schedule), what's done with the present perfect (We've completed the design), what's happening now with the present continuous (We're currently working on the payment page), the next step (The next step is to …) and the main risk (The main risk is that …). With a finished time, use the past simple: We finished the design last week. Say in progress, not 'on progress'.

examples.en: Overall, we're on track for the June launch.
examples.id: Secara keseluruhan, kami sesuai rencana untuk peluncuran bulan Juni.

examples.en: We've completed the user testing, and we're currently fixing the bugs.
examples.id: Kami sudah menyelesaikan uji coba pengguna, dan saat ini sedang memperbaiki bug-nya.

examples.en: The main risk is that the supplier might be late.
examples.id: Risiko utamanya adalah pemasoknya mungkin terlambat.

id.title: Menyampaikan update perkembangan dengan jelas
id.explanation: Update yang jelas punya sampai lima bagian: statusnya (We're on track / slightly behind schedule), yang sudah selesai dengan present perfect (We've completed the design), yang sedang dikerjakan dengan present continuous (We're currently working on the payment page), langkah berikutnya (The next step is to …) dan risiko utamanya (The main risk is that …). Kalau ada waktu yang sudah lewat, pakai past simple: We finished the design last week. Katakan in progress, bukan 'on progress'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Bu Ani is talking about the new office in Bandung. You want to add an idea. Complete with one word: Sorry, could I just ___ something here?
You're explaining your plan, and Dimas starts asking questions before you're done. Complete with one word: Just let me ___ this point.
Pak Hasan says: 'Let's start with a soft launch.' You don't know what a soft launch is. Complete with one word: Sorry, could you ___ what you mean by a soft launch?
guidedPractice.hint: memperjelas = … (it looks like the Indonesian klarifikasi).

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete the update with one word: We've finished the design. The ___ step is to test the app with real users.
Complete the update with one word: Right now, we're working ___ the payment page.

independentPractice.prompt: At the end of the meeting, you repeat the tasks: who does what, and by when. Complete with one word: Let me ___ the action points.
independentPractice.hint: In Indonesian offices people say 'rekap' too.

independentPractice.prompt: Tell your team the biggest problem that could happen: the supplier might be late. Complete with one word: The main ___ is that the supplier might be late.
The team is discussing the budget, and you want to join. Complete with one word: If I could just come ___ here, I think the budget is too small.
independentPractice.hint: come … = ikut bicara, masuk ke diskusi

assessment.prompt: In a project meeting, Pak Hasan is talking about the launch date. You have an important point about the budget and can't wait until the end. Complete the polite interruption with one word: Sorry to ___, but could I just add something about the budget?
assessment.rubric: Correct: interrupt (Sorry to interrupt, but …). 'cut in' and 'jump in' are also correct = 100. 'butt in' = 50 (understood, but informal and a bit rude-sounding). 'disturb' or 'bother you' = 60 (understood, but in a meeting you interrupt a speaker). 'cut' alone = 20 (the node's common error, from 'saya potong': cut alone means memotong). 'interrupting' = 70 (Sorry to needs the base form).

assessment.prompt: You're sharing your screen in a Zoom meeting to show the sales figures, but the file is opening very slowly. Ask everyone to wait patiently for a moment. Complete with one word: ___ with me for a second.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Bear with me for a second (= please wait patiently). 'bare' = 70 (the right word said aloud, but the wrong spelling: bare means kosong / telanjang). 'wait' or 'stay' = 30 ('Wait with me' and 'Stay with me' aren't the phrase; 'Please wait a second' would be fine as a different sentence).

assessment.prompt: In the meeting, Bu Ani mentioned both Thursday and Friday for the client meeting, and now you're not sure which day it is. Check it. Complete with one word: Just to be ___, the client meeting is on Thursday, not Friday?
assessment.rubric: Correct: clear (Just to be clear, …?). 'sure' and 'certain' are also correct = 100. 'clarify' = 40 ('Just to clarify' is a good phrase, but after 'to be' you need an adjective: clear). 'confirm' = 40 (same problem: 'Just to confirm' works, 'Just to be confirm' doesn't).

assessment.prompt: For five minutes, Pak Hasan explains that the company has less money this year and can't hire new staff until January. Check that you've understood by saying it back. Complete with one word: So what you're ___ is that we can't hire anyone new until January?
assessment.rubric: Correct: saying (So what you're saying is …?). 'telling us' / 'telling me' = 100. 'suggesting' = 70 (good English, but Pak Hasan is stating a fact, not making a suggestion). 'meaning' = 60 (understood, but the natural form is 'what you mean is', without 'are'). 'say' = 50 (after you're, use the -ing form). 'talking' = 30.

assessment.prompt: At the end of the meeting, you repeat the main decisions in a few words. Complete with one word: So, to ___ up: Sari will update the website, and Budi will call the client by Friday.
assessment.rubric: Correct: sum (So, to sum up, …). 'wrap' (to wrap up) = 100. 'summarise' / 'summarize' = 50 (a good verb, but it doesn't take 'up': say 'So, to summarise, …'). 'conclude' = 30. 'some' = 70 (heard right, spelled wrong).

assessment.prompt: Your team should finish the new app this Friday, but you need one more week. Give the status honestly in the Monday meeting. Complete with one word: We're about a week ___ schedule.
assessment.rubric: Correct: behind (a week behind schedule = terlambat seminggu dari jadwal). 'ahead of' = 0 (that means earlier than planned). 'late' = 30 (We're a week late is fine, but 'late schedule' isn't). 'behind of' = 60 (no 'of' after behind).

assessment.prompt: Your project has five milestones, and your team has done three of them. Complete the update with the verb finish in the right form: So far, we ___ three of the five milestones.
assessment.rubric: Correct: have finished (So far → present perfect: done up to now, no finished time). 'finished' = 50 (past simple doesn't fit 'so far'). 'have finish' = 40 (have + the third form: finished). 'already finish' or 'finish' = 20 (no tense marking, from 'sudah selesai'). 'are finishing' = 20.

material.title: Interrupting politely and holding the floor

blocks.text:
Quick recap: in discussions you learnt to take turns and invite others (*What do you think, Sari?*), and to disagree softly (*I see what you mean, but …*). In a meeting you sometimes can't wait for your turn: the topic is about to change, or there's a mistake in the numbers. Then you **interrupt** (menyela) politely, in three parts:
- a **soft start**: ***Sorry to interrupt, but …*** / ***Sorry to jump in, but …*** (a bit more relaxed)
- a **small request**: ***Could I just add something?*** / ***If I could just come in here, …*** (a phrase to remember: *come in* = ikut bicara, masuk ke diskusi)
- then **your point, quickly**.

The little word **just** (cuma, sebentar saja) makes your request sound small, so it's easier to say yes.

**Holding the floor** (mempertahankan giliran bicara) is the other side: someone interrupts you, but you want to finish first.
- ***Just let me finish this point.***
- ***Bear with me for a second.*** (mohon sabar sebentar) *bear* here means 'tahan, sabar', nothing to do with the animal, and it's spelled *bear*, not *bare*.
- ***I'll come to that in a minute.*** (nanti saya bahas)

When you've finished, give the turn back: ***Sorry, go ahead.*** (silakan)

id.text:
Ulasan singkat: di pelajaran diskusi kamu belajar bergiliran dan mengajak orang lain bicara (*What do you think, Sari?*), dan tidak setuju dengan halus (*I see what you mean, but …*). Dalam rapat, kadang kamu tidak bisa menunggu giliran: topiknya akan segera berganti, atau ada kesalahan di angkanya. Saat itu kamu **interrupt** (menyela) dengan sopan, dalam tiga bagian:
- **pembuka yang halus**: ***Sorry to interrupt, but …*** / ***Sorry to jump in, but …*** (sedikit lebih santai)
- **permintaan kecil**: ***Could I just add something?*** / ***If I could just come in here, …*** (ungkapan untuk dihafal: *come in* = ikut bicara, masuk ke diskusi)
- lalu **poinmu, dengan cepat**.

Kata kecil **just** (cuma, sebentar saja) membuat permintaanmu terdengar kecil, jadi lebih mudah dijawab ya.

**Holding the floor** (mempertahankan giliran bicara) adalah sisi sebaliknya: seseorang menyelamu, tapi kamu ingin selesai dulu.
- ***Just let me finish this point.*** (biarkan saya selesaikan poin ini dulu)
- ***Bear with me for a second.*** (mohon sabar sebentar) *bear* di sini artinya 'tahan, sabar', tidak ada hubungannya dengan beruang, dan ditulis *bear*, bukan *bare*.
- ***I'll come to that in a minute.*** (nanti saya bahas)

Setelah selesai, kembalikan gilirannya: ***Sorry, go ahead.*** (silakan)

rows.en: Sorry to interrupt, but could I just add something? The 17th is a public holiday.
rows.id: Maaf menyela, tapi boleh saya menambahkan sesuatu? Tanggal 17 itu hari libur nasional.

rows.en: If I could just come in here, the client already said no to that idea.
rows.id: Kalau boleh saya ikut bicara, kliennya sudah menolak ide itu.
rows.note: a phrase to remember: learn it as one piece

id.note: ungkapan untuk dihafal: pelajari sebagai satu kesatuan

rows.en: Sorry to jump in, but we only have ten minutes left.
rows.id: Maaf memotong, tapi waktu kita tinggal sepuluh menit.

rows.en: Good question, Budi. I'll come to that in a minute.
rows.id: Pertanyaan bagus, Budi. Nanti saya bahas sebentar lagi.

rows.en: OK, that's my point. Sorry, Sari, go ahead.
rows.id: Oke, itu poin saya. Maaf, Sari, silakan.

blocks.text:
Two Indonesian traps:
- **'Maaf, saya potong' is not `Sorry, I want to cut` ✗.** In English, *cut* alone means memotong (kertas, biaya). Say **Sorry to interrupt, but …** (the phrasal verb *cut in* does exist: *Sorry to cut in* is fine). *I want to …* also sounds like a demand. *Sorry before* (maaf sebelumnya) isn't English either.
- **Silence isn't polite in an English meeting.** Many of us wait until the boss or an older colleague has finished (sungkan). In English meetings, a short, polite interruption with a good reason is normal, and saying nothing is often taken as agreement. But *Wait! Stop! Don't cut me!* is far too direct.

id.text:
Dua jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia:
- **'Maaf, saya potong' bukan `Sorry, I want to cut` ✗.** Dalam bahasa Inggris, *cut* saja artinya memotong (kertas, biaya). Katakan **Sorry to interrupt, but …** (phrasal verb *cut in* memang ada: *Sorry to cut in* boleh). *I want to …* juga terdengar seperti menuntut. *Sorry before* (maaf sebelumnya) juga bukan bahasa Inggris.
- **Diam itu tidak sopan di rapat berbahasa Inggris.** Banyak dari kita menunggu sampai atasan atau rekan yang lebih senior selesai bicara (sungkan). Di rapat berbahasa Inggris, menyela sebentar dengan sopan dan dengan alasan yang jelas itu wajar, dan diam sering dianggap setuju. Tapi *Wait! Stop! Don't cut me!* jauh terlalu langsung.

blocks.prompt: Pak Hasan says the deadline is the 15th, but you know the client changed it to the 10th. Which interruption sounds polite and clear?
options: Sorry, I want to cut. Wrong date.
Sorry to interrupt, but the client moved the deadline to the 10th.
Sorry before, maybe, if possible, the date …
blocks.explain: It has a soft start (*Sorry to interrupt, but*) and then the point, quickly and clearly. *I want to cut* is the Indonesian *saya potong* word for word and sounds like a demand; the third one never says the point.

id.prompt: Pak Hasan bilang tenggatnya tanggal 15, tapi kamu tahu kliennya sudah mengubahnya ke tanggal 10. Selaan mana yang terdengar sopan dan jelas?
id.explain: Ada pembuka yang halus (*Sorry to interrupt, but*) lalu poinnya, cepat dan jelas. *I want to cut* adalah terjemahan kata per kata dari *saya potong* dan terdengar seperti menuntut; pilihan ketiga tidak pernah menyebut poinnya.

id.title: Menyela dengan sopan dan mempertahankan giliran bicara

blocks.text:
**Clarify** (memperjelas; it looks like *klarifikasi*) when a word or an idea isn't clear. Ask about the exact word with **by**:
- ***Sorry, could you clarify what you mean by …?***
- ***What exactly do you mean by …?***
- ***Sorry, I'm not sure I follow.*** (maaf, saya kurang menangkap)

**Check your understanding** by saying the idea back in your own words. The other person can then say *Yes, exactly* or correct you:
- ***So what you're saying is …?***
- ***Just to be clear, …?*** (*Just to be sure* is also fine)

**Summarise** at the end of a topic or a meeting, so everyone leaves with the same picture:
- ***So, to sum up, …*** (jadi, singkatnya …)
- ***Let me recap the action points.*** (*recap* = rekap: who does what, by when)
- ***Let's go over the action points.***

Spelling: *summarise* (British) / *summarize* (American).

id.text:
**Clarify** (memperjelas; mirip *klarifikasi*) saat sebuah kata atau ide tidak jelas. Tanyakan kata yang persis dengan **by**:
- ***Sorry, could you clarify what you mean by …?*** (maaf, bisa diperjelas apa maksud Anda dengan …?)
- ***What exactly do you mean by …?*** (maksudnya … itu apa persisnya?)
- ***Sorry, I'm not sure I follow.*** (maaf, saya kurang menangkap)

**Cek pemahamanmu** dengan mengulang idenya pakai kata-katamu sendiri. Orang itu lalu bisa bilang *Yes, exactly* atau membetulkanmu:
- ***So what you're saying is …?*** (jadi maksud Anda …?)
- ***Just to be clear, …?*** (biar jelas, …?) (*Just to be sure* juga boleh)

**Rangkum** di akhir sebuah topik atau rapat, supaya semua orang pulang dengan gambaran yang sama:
- ***So, to sum up, …*** (jadi, singkatnya …)
- ***Let me recap the action points.*** (*recap* = rekap: siapa melakukan apa, sampai kapan)
- ***Let's go over the action points.*** (mari kita bahas lagi poin tindak lanjutnya)

Ejaan: *summarise* (British) / *summarize* (Amerika).

rows.en: Sorry, could you clarify what you mean by 'a lighter version'?
rows.id: Maaf, bisa diperjelas apa maksud Anda dengan 'versi yang lebih ringan'?

rows.en: What exactly do you mean by 'soon'? This week or this month?
rows.id: Maksudnya 'segera' itu apa persisnya? Minggu ini atau bulan ini?

rows.en: So what you're saying is that we need two more designers?
rows.id: Jadi maksud Anda, kita butuh dua desainer lagi?

rows.en: Just to be clear, the budget includes the hotel?
rows.id: Biar jelas, anggarannya sudah termasuk hotel?

rows.en: So, to sum up, we're going to test the app in Surabaya first.
rows.id: Jadi, singkatnya, kita akan menguji aplikasinya di Surabaya dulu.

blocks.text:
Three traps:
- **'Maksudnya?' is not `Meaning?` ✗.** That sounds blunt. And *What do you mean?* on its own, with a flat voice, can sound like a challenge (*apa maksudmu?!*). Add *Sorry* and the word: **Sorry, what do you mean by 'phase two'?**
- **`Can you repeat again?` ✗.** *repeat* already means 'say again'. Say **Could you say that again?** or **Could you repeat that?**
- **In conclusion** is for essays and formal speeches. At the end of a meeting, **So, to sum up, …** sounds more natural. (It's a tendency, not a strict rule.)

id.text:
Tiga jebakan:
- **'Maksudnya?' bukan `Meaning?` ✗.** Itu terdengar ketus. Dan *What do you mean?* saja, dengan nada datar, bisa terdengar menantang (*apa maksudmu?!*). Tambahkan *Sorry* dan katanya: **Sorry, what do you mean by 'phase two'?**
- **`Can you repeat again?` ✗.** *repeat* sudah berarti 'mengatakan lagi'. Katakan **Could you say that again?** atau **Could you repeat that?**
- **In conclusion** untuk esai dan pidato resmi. Di akhir rapat, **So, to sum up, …** terdengar lebih wajar. (Ini kecenderungan, bukan aturan ketat.)

blocks.prompt: Your manager says the team needs 'more ownership'. You don't understand what she means. What's the best thing to say?
options: Sorry, could you clarify what you mean by 'more ownership'?
blocks.explain: It's polite (*Sorry*) and asks about the exact words with *clarify what you mean by*. *Meaning?* is the Indonesian *Maksudnya?* and sounds blunt. *Can you repeat again?* says 'again' twice, and hearing the same words again won't explain them.

id.prompt: Manajermu bilang timnya butuh 'more ownership'. Kamu tidak paham maksudnya. Apa yang paling baik untuk dikatakan?
id.explain: Kalimat ini sopan (*Sorry*) dan menanyakan kata yang persis dengan *clarify what you mean by*. *Meaning?* adalah *Maksudnya?* versi Indonesia dan terdengar ketus. *Can you repeat again?* mengatakan 'lagi' dua kali, dan mendengar kata yang sama lagi tidak akan menjelaskan artinya.

blocks.text:
In a weekly meeting or a daily stand-up (rapat singkat harian), your manager asks: *Can you give us a quick update on the app?* A clear update has up to five parts, each with its own verb form:
- **Status:** ***We're on track.*** / ***We're slightly behind schedule.*** / ***We're ahead of schedule.***
- **Done** (present perfect, no finished time): ***We've completed the design.*** / ***We've already tested it on Android.***
- **Now** (present continuous): ***We're currently working on the payment page.*** / ***We're waiting for the client's feedback.***
- **Next:** ***The next step is to …*** / ***Next week we're going to …***
- **Risk:** ***The main risk is that …*** (+ *might*: *the supplier might be late*)

With a **finished time** (*last week, yesterday, on Monday*), use the **past simple**: *We **finished** the design last week* (not *We've finished it last week*). It's the same rule as in the present perfect lesson.

**progress** is uncountable (tidak bisa dihitung): *We've made **good progress***, not *a good progress* or *progresses*.

id.text:
Di rapat mingguan atau daily stand-up (rapat singkat harian), manajermu bertanya: *Can you give us a quick update on the app?* Update yang jelas punya sampai lima bagian, masing-masing dengan bentuk kata kerjanya sendiri:
- **Status:** ***We're on track.*** (sesuai rencana) / ***We're slightly behind schedule.*** (sedikit terlambat dari jadwal) / ***We're ahead of schedule.*** (lebih cepat dari jadwal)
- **Sudah selesai** (present perfect, tanpa waktu yang sudah lewat): ***We've completed the design.*** / ***We've already tested it on Android.***
- **Sedang dikerjakan** (present continuous): ***We're currently working on the payment page.*** / ***We're waiting for the client's feedback.***
- **Berikutnya:** ***The next step is to …*** / ***Next week we're going to …***
- **Risiko:** ***The main risk is that …*** (+ *might*: *the supplier might be late*)

Kalau ada **waktu yang sudah lewat** (*last week, yesterday, on Monday*), pakai **past simple**: *We **finished** the design last week* (bukan *We've finished it last week*). Aturannya sama seperti di pelajaran present perfect.

**progress** tidak bisa dihitung (uncountable): *We've made **good progress***, bukan *a good progress* atau *progresses*.

rows.en: Quick update on the website: we're on track for the launch in June.
rows.id: Update singkat soal website: kami sesuai rencana untuk peluncuran bulan Juni.

rows.en: We've finished the home page, and we're currently working on the shop.
rows.id: Kami sudah menyelesaikan halaman utama, dan saat ini sedang mengerjakan bagian toko.

rows.en: We tested the app with twenty users last week.
rows.id: Kami menguji aplikasinya dengan dua puluh pengguna minggu lalu.
rows.note: last week = a finished time, so past simple

id.note: last week = waktu yang sudah lewat, jadi past simple

rows.en: The next step is to fix the bugs they found.
rows.id: Langkah berikutnya adalah memperbaiki bug yang mereka temukan.

rows.en: The main risk is that the payment provider might not be ready.
rows.id: Risiko utamanya adalah penyedia pembayarannya mungkin belum siap.

rows.en: It's still in progress. We've made good progress, though.
rows.id: Masih dalam proses. Tapi kami sudah ada kemajuan yang bagus.

blocks.text:
Indonesian office traps:
- **`Masih on progress` ✗.** Very common in Indonesian offices, but English says **It's still in progress** or **We're still working on it.**
- **No tense marking.** *sudah selesai* → `We already finish` ✗ → **We've already finished.** *sedang* → be + -ing: `We working on it` ✗ → **We're working on it.**
- **actually ≠ saat ini.** Indonesian *aktual* means 'terkini', but English *actually* means *sebenarnya*. For 'saat ini', say **currently** or **at the moment**.
- **British vs American:** Americans often say *We already finished it* (past simple + already). You'll hear it; the present perfect works everywhere.

id.text:
Jebakan dari kantor di Indonesia:
- **`Masih on progress` ✗.** Sangat umum di kantor-kantor Indonesia, tapi dalam bahasa Inggris yang benar **It's still in progress** atau **We're still working on it.**
- **Tanpa penanda waktu.** *sudah selesai* → `We already finish` ✗ → **We've already finished.** *sedang* → be + -ing: `We working on it` ✗ → **We're working on it.**
- **actually ≠ saat ini.** *aktual* dalam bahasa Indonesia berarti 'terkini', tapi *actually* dalam bahasa Inggris berarti *sebenarnya*. Untuk 'saat ini', katakan **currently** atau **at the moment**.
- **British vs Amerika:** orang Amerika sering bilang *We already finished it* (past simple + already). Kamu akan mendengarnya; present perfect bisa dipakai di mana saja.

blocks.prompt: Your manager asks about the monthly report. It isn't finished: you're still writing it. Which answer is correct English?
blocks.explain: Something that has started but isn't finished is **in progress** (dalam proses). *On progress* is a very common Indonesian office mistake, and *progressing on* isn't English.

id.prompt: Manajermu bertanya soal laporan bulanan. Laporannya belum selesai: kamu masih menulisnya. Jawaban mana yang benar dalam bahasa Inggris?
id.explain: Sesuatu yang sudah dimulai tapi belum selesai disebut **in progress** (dalam proses). *On progress* adalah kesalahan yang sangat umum di kantor-kantor Indonesia, dan *progressing on* bukan bahasa Inggris.

blocks.text:
Online meetings add a few problems. Recap from the calls lesson: ***You're on mute*** (mic-mu masih mati), ***Sorry, you're breaking up*** (suaramu putus-putus), ***Could you say that again?*** Two more:
- ***Can everyone see my screen?*** (layar saya kelihatan?) when you share your screen.
- When two people start talking at the same time: ***Sorry, go ahead.*** / ***No, you go first.***

Here's a short Zoom stand-up at a startup in Jakarta. Find the interruption, the clarification, the update and the summary.

id.text:
Rapat online punya beberapa masalah tambahan. Ulasan dari pelajaran telepon: ***You're on mute*** (mic-mu masih mati), ***Sorry, you're breaking up*** (suaramu putus-putus), ***Could you say that again?*** (bisa diulang?) Dua lagi:
- ***Can everyone see my screen?*** (layar saya kelihatan?) saat kamu berbagi layar.
- Saat dua orang mulai bicara bersamaan: ***Sorry, go ahead.*** (maaf, silakan) / ***No, you go first.*** (tidak, kamu duluan)

Ini rapat stand-up singkat di Zoom di sebuah startup di Jakarta. Temukan selaan, klarifikasi, update dan rangkumannya.

rows.en: Rina: Quick update: we're slightly behind schedule. We've finished the login page, and we're currently working on payments.
rows.id: Rina: Update singkat: kami sedikit terlambat dari jadwal. Kami sudah menyelesaikan halaman login, dan saat ini sedang mengerjakan pembayaran.

rows.en: Budi: Sorry to interrupt, Rina, but what exactly do you mean by 'slightly'?
rows.id: Budi: Maaf menyela, Rina, tapi 'sedikit' itu maksudnya persisnya berapa?

rows.en: Rina: About three days. Bear with me, I'll share the plan. Can everyone see my screen?
rows.id: Rina: Sekitar tiga hari. Mohon sabar, saya bagikan rencananya. Layar saya kelihatan semua?

rows.en: Pak Hasan: Yes. So what you're saying is that we can still launch on the 20th?
rows.id: Pak Hasan: Ya. Jadi maksudmu kita masih bisa meluncurkan tanggal 20?

rows.en: Rina: Yes, if the bank answers this week. That's the main risk.
rows.id: Rina: Ya, kalau pihak bank menjawab minggu ini. Itu risiko utamanya.

rows.en: Pak Hasan: OK, to sum up: Rina will call the bank today, and we'll check again on Friday.
rows.id: Pak Hasan: Oke, singkatnya: Rina akan menelepon pihak bank hari ini, dan kita cek lagi hari Jumat.

blocks.prompt: In a Google Meet call, you and Dimas start talking at exactly the same time. What's a polite thing to say?
blocks.explain: When two people start at once, offer the turn: **Sorry, go ahead** (or *No, you go first*). *You're on mute* is for someone you can't hear at all, and *Can everyone see my screen?* is for sharing your screen.

id.prompt: Di panggilan Google Meet, kamu dan Dimas mulai bicara tepat bersamaan. Apa yang sopan untuk dikatakan?
id.explain: Kalau dua orang mulai bersamaan, tawarkan gilirannya: **Sorry, go ahead** (atau *No, you go first*). *You're on mute* untuk orang yang suaranya sama sekali tidak terdengar, dan *Can everyone see my screen?* untuk saat berbagi layar.

assessment.mtg-1: Dalam rapat proyek, Pak Hasan sedang membahas tanggal peluncuran. Kamu punya poin penting soal anggaran dan tidak bisa menunggu sampai akhir. Lengkapi selaan yang sopan ini dengan satu kata: Sorry to ___, but could I just add something about the budget?
assessment.mtg-2: Kamu sedang berbagi layar di rapat Zoom untuk menunjukkan angka penjualan, tapi filenya terbuka sangat lambat. Minta semua orang menunggu dengan sabar sebentar. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: ___ with me for a second.
assessment.mtg-3: Dalam rapat, Bu Ani menyebut hari Kamis dan Jumat untuk rapat dengan klien, dan sekarang kamu tidak yakin harinya yang mana. Cek dulu. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: Just to be ___, the client meeting is on Thursday, not Friday?
assessment.mtg-4: Selama lima menit, Pak Hasan menjelaskan bahwa uang perusahaan tahun ini lebih sedikit dan belum bisa merekrut karyawan baru sampai Januari. Cek bahwa kamu sudah paham dengan mengulanginya. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: So what you're ___ is that we can't hire anyone new until January?
assessment.mtg-5: Di akhir rapat, kamu mengulang keputusan utamanya dengan singkat. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: So, to ___ up: Sari will update the website, and Budi will call the client by Friday.
assessment.mtg-6: Timmu seharusnya menyelesaikan aplikasi baru hari Jumat ini, tapi kalian butuh satu minggu lagi. Sampaikan statusnya dengan jujur di rapat hari Senin. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: We're about a week ___ schedule.
assessment.mtg-7: Proyekmu punya lima tahap penting (milestones), dan timmu sudah menyelesaikan tiga di antaranya. Lengkapi update ini dengan kata kerja finish dalam bentuk yang tepat: So far, we ___ three of the five milestones.
